pi0fast-native.acceptance_reason: Not accepted for validated paired stage comparison: output exact/allclose fails, including22 of25 same-seed pairs between both uninstrumented baselines. Native baseline timings and instrumented stages remain descriptive, with uncontrolled generated work across conditions.

conclusions.smol_pi05_ranking: Uninstrumented call ranges do not overlap in this isolated run: Smol518.106–689.627ms versus Pi05299.828–429.258ms; pooled means603.573ms versus367.896ms.
conclusions.smol_pi05_main_stage_finding: Instrumented action denoising dominates: CUDA stream intervals497.574ms Smol versus230.974ms Pi05. Vision intervals18.166ms versus18.942ms overlap strongly. This localizes the large observed difference to action generation and contradicts512px vision being the main cost in this run.
conclusions.fast_failure_finding: Both uninstrumented baselines differ in22 of25 exact same-input/same-seed pairs, so instrumentation alone is not established as the cause. Native execution is not reproducible under the recorded protocol. Preserve the failed output-equivalence check.
limitations: This is an isolated offline timing experiment, not a new task-success or realtime-control evaluation.
Instrumented stage differences do not exactly decompose the historical realtime latency or the uninstrumented mean gap.
B-I-B timing variation and drift prevent small stage differences or negative timing contrasts from being interpreted as optimization effects.
Stored parameter dtype differs from representative compute dtype; Smol is not allFP32.
Stage timing does not prove that layer count, kernel implementation, dispatch overhead, precision, or camera batching alone causes the observed difference.
FAST baseline token IDs/counts were not captured; matched generated workload and arithmetic-preserving instrumentation are unproven.
CUDA event elapsed and host wall time cannot be subtracted to isolate CPU overhead.
